cls: Anti-obesity agent (selective serotonin 5-HT2C receptor agonist); Schedule IV controlled substance - WITHDRAWN from US market
pharm: Lorcaserin is a selective agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2C receptor in the hypothalamus. Activation of 5-HT2C receptors on anorexigenic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons is believed to promote satiety and reduce food intake. Selectivity for 5-HT2C over the 5-HT2B (cardiac valve) and 5-HT2A (CNS/hallucinogenic) receptors was intended to avoid the valvulopathy seen with earlier non-selective serotonergic appetite suppressants.
quick: Historically 10 mg twice daily (BELVIQ IR) or 20 mg once daily (BELVIQ XR) - product WITHDRAWN, no longer marketed
Could be taken with or without food
Contraindicated - weight loss offers no benefit and may harm the fetus; pregnancy was a contraindication
Avoid - not recommended; unknown if excreted in human milk
Use with caution in severe impairment; XR not recommended in severe renal impairment / ESRD
Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment
Avoid - additive CNS depression/sedation and impaired judgment
Weight loss response (discontinue if <5% by week 12), serotonin syndrome, mood/suicidality, signs of valvular heart disease
summary: Lorcaserin (BELVIQ and extended-release BELVIQ XR) was a selective serotonin 5-HT2C receptor agonist approved as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with obesity (BMI >=30) or overweight (BMI >=27) with at least one weight-related comorbidity. It was a Schedule IV controlled substance. In February 2020 the FDA requested its withdrawal from the US market after the long-term cardiovascular safety trial CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 showed a higher incidence of cancer (including pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers) among patients taking lorcaserin than placebo, leading the FDA to conclude the potential risks outweighed the benefits. Lorcaserin is therefore NO LONGER available, is not in current FDA/openFDA active labeling, and should not be prescribed. As a serotonergic drug it carried risks of serotonin syndrome and neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reactions, especially when combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, triptans, or other serotonergic agents. Therapy was to be stopped if at least 5% of baseline body weight was not lost by week 12.
indications: Adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with an initial BMI >=30 kg/m2 (obese), or >=27 kg/m2 (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbidity such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, or type 2 diabetes
NOTE: This indication is HISTORICAL - the product was withdrawn from the US market in February 2020 and is no longer available or recommended

admin: PRODUCT WITHDRAWN - the following reflects historical administration before the February 2020 US-market withdrawal
Immediate-release (BELVIQ): 10 mg taken twice daily, with or without food
Extended-release (BELVIQ XR): 20 mg once daily; swallow whole and do not cut, crush, or chew
Used only as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
Evaluate weight loss at 12 weeks; discontinue if <5% of baseline weight lost
As a Schedule IV controlled substance, dispensing was subject to controlled-substance regulations
moa: Lorcaserin is a selective agonist of the 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C (5-HT2C) serotonin receptor. By preferentially activating 5-HT2C receptors on anorexigenic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus, it is thought to increase satiety and decrease food intake, producing weight loss. Its relative selectivity for 5-HT2C over the 5-HT2B receptor (expressed on cardiac valves and implicated in valvulopathy from older non-selective serotonergic agents such as fenfluramine) and over the 5-HT2A receptor (associated with hallucinogenic and CNS effects) was the basis for its intended improved safety profile. The exact mechanism by which it caused the increased cancer incidence observed in long-term cardiovascular outcome data is not established.

absolute: Pregnancy (weight loss provides no benefit and may cause fetal harm)
Known hypersensitivity to lorcaserin or any product component
relative: Concomitant serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, triptans, bupropion, dextromethorphan, St. John's wort) - serotonin syndrome / NMS-like risk
Pre-existing valvular heart disease or congestive heart failure
Severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease (especially XR)
Men at risk for priapism or with conditions predisposing to priapism
monitor: Achievement of >=5% weight loss by week 12
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome or NMS-like reactions
New or worsening depression, mood changes, or suicidal thoughts
Signs/symptoms of valvular heart disease (dyspnea, edema, heart murmur)
Heart rate (bradycardia) and, in patients with diabetes, blood glucose/hypoglycemia

preg: Pregnancy was a contraindication. Weight loss offers no potential benefit to a pregnant woman and may result in fetal harm; lorcaserin should not be used during pregnancy. Animal data showed developmental toxicity. A patient who becomes pregnant should discontinue the drug. (Product is withdrawn and should not be used regardless.)
lact: It is not known whether lorcaserin is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant and the lack of clinical need for weight loss during lactation, breastfeeding was not recommended during treatment. (Product is withdrawn.)
renal: Lorcaserin should be used with caution in patients with renal impairment. The extended-release formulation (BELVIQ XR) was not recommended in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease. Active metabolites can accumulate; monitor for adverse effects. (Product is withdrawn.)
hepatic: No dose adjustment was required for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Lorcaserin should be used with caution in patients with severe hepatic impairment, as exposure data were limited. (Product is withdrawn.)

major: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) - high risk of serotonin syndrome / hypertensive reactions
SSRIs and SNRIs - increased risk of serotonin syndrome
Triptans, ergot derivatives - increased risk of serotonin syndrome
Bupropion, dextromethorphan, lithium, tramadol, St. John's wort, other serotonergic agents - serotonin syndrome risk
Antipsychotics / dopamine antagonists - risk of NMS-like reactions
moderate: CYP2D6 substrates (e.g., dextromethorphan) - lorcaserin can increase exposure as a weak CYP2D6 inhibitor
Antidiabetic agents (insulin, sulfonylureas) - increased hypoglycemia risk with weight loss; may need dose reduction
Other CNS depressants - additive sedation and dizziness
minor: Agents associated with priapism (e.g., PDE5 inhibitors, antipsychotics) - additive priapism risk
interactions.food: Could be administered with or without food; food did not meaningfully limit clinical use.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - additive central nervous system depression, sedation, dizziness, and impaired judgment.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood glucose in patients with type 2 diabetes (hypoglycemia risk as weight is lost); no characteristic laboratory assay interference is established.

serious: New or worsening depression and suicidal ideation
Cognitive impairment (confusion, difficulty concentrating, memory problems)
Severe hypoglycemia in patients on antidiabetic therapy
Increased incidence of cancer with long-term use (CAMELLIA-TIMI 61)
emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Weight loss response - discontinue if at least 5% of baseline body weight is not lost by week 12
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome and NMS-like reactions, especially with concomitant serotonergic drugs
Mood, depression, and emergence of suicidal ideation or behavior
Signs/symptoms of valvular heart disease (echocardiography if symptoms develop)
Blood glucose in patients with type 2 diabetes (hypoglycemia)
Complete blood count and prolactin if clinically indicated
counsel: IMPORTANT: This medicine has been removed from the US market - it is no longer available and should not be taken
If you still have this medicine, stop using it and talk to your pharmacist or doctor about safe disposal
It was withdrawn because a long-term study found more cases of cancer in people who took it
Tell your doctor about any antidepressants, migraine medicines, or other drugs you take, because of the risk of a serious reaction called serotonin syndrome
Seek emergency care for agitation, fever, fast heartbeat, muscle stiffness, an erection lasting more than 4 hours, or thoughts of self-harm
Discuss other evidence-based options for weight management with your healthcare provider
pk: Appetite/satiety effect within hours; meaningful weight loss over weeks
Plasma Tmax ~1.5-2 hours for immediate-release; later for extended-release
Immediate-release dosed twice daily; extended-release once daily
Was stored at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted) - product withdrawn
pearls: WITHDRAWN: At FDA request, lorcaserin (BELVIQ / BELVIQ XR) was removed from the US market in February 2020 - do NOT prescribe or use
Withdrawal was driven by an increased incidence of cancer (pancreatic, colorectal, lung) in the long-term cardiovascular safety trial CAMELLIA-TIMI 61
It was a Schedule IV controlled substance and a selective 5-HT2C receptor agonist
Serotonergic: risk of serotonin syndrome and NMS-like reactions, especially with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs/triptans
Historical rule: discontinue if <5% of baseline body weight was not lost by week 12
5-HT2C selectivity over 5-HT2B was intended to avoid the valvulopathy seen with fenfluramine, but valvular monitoring was still advised
missed: Not applicable - lorcaserin has been withdrawn from the US market and should no longer be used. Historically, a missed dose was to be skipped and the regular schedule resumed without doubling up; patients who still possess the drug should stop taking it and consult a healthcare professional.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Management is symptomatic and supportive, with attention to serotonergic toxicity (serotonin syndrome). Monitor cardiovascular status, mental status, and vital signs; provide supportive care, consider activated charcoal for recent ingestion if airway is protected, and contact a poison control center. Treat serotonin syndrome with cooling, benzodiazepines, and supportive measures as indicated.
